quests.hint: You're overloaded with work.
quests.explanation: "Swamped" is a friendly, informal way to say you have far too much to do. It's very common at work.
quests.meaning: An informal way to say you're very busy.
quests.sampleUsage: I'm swamped this week, so I can't join lunch.
quests.instruction: Say it with a tired sigh.
quests.situationExample: A classmate invites you to coffee while you're finishing a huge project.

quests.hint: You're physically or mentally tired.
quests.explanation: Used after a long day or intense activity. Register: casual, clear.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying you're very tired.
quests.sampleUsage: I'm worn out after standing all day.
quests.instruction: Say it with a tired voice.
quests.situationExample: You reach home after a long day of standing at work.

quests.hint: You have very little energy left.
quests.explanation: It compares yourself to a car with no fuel. Useful when you're exhausted but still going.
quests.meaning: An idiom meaning you have almost no energy.
quests.sampleUsage: I've been up since five, so I'm running on empty.
quests.instruction: Say it with a tired, humorous tone.
quests.situationExample: It's late afternoon and you haven't had lunch or a break.

quests.hint: Months seem to vanish quickly.
quests.explanation: People say it at birthdays, reunions and holidays.
quests.meaning: A phrase showing that time passes quickly.
quests.sampleUsage: Wow, it's already December. Time flies!
quests.instruction: Say it with a slightly surprised tone.
quests.situationExample: You realize your first year at a new job has finished.

quests.hint: It arrived after the expected time, but you're glad it arrived at all.
quests.explanation: Don't use it to criticize someone harshly. The feel is friendly and light.
quests.meaning: An idiom saying that doing something late is better than not at all.
quests.sampleUsage: You finally sent me a birthday message? Better late than never.
quests.instruction: Say it kindly, in a playful tone.
quests.situationExample: A friend finally sends a birthday message two days late.

quests.hint: Something happened right before a deadline.
quests.explanation: It often shows relief after a close call. The feel is simple and easy.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying something happened at the last possible moment.
quests.sampleUsage: We got to the station just in time for the last train.
quests.instruction: Say it with relief.
quests.situationExample: You run into the station as the doors are about to close.

quests.hint: Something is very easy.
quests.explanation: In tone it's informal and popular. Use it for tasks, tests or activities that felt simple.
quests.meaning: An idiom meaning something is very easy.
quests.sampleUsage: The quiz was a piece of cake.
quests.instruction: Say it confidently, with a smile.
quests.situationExample: You come out of an easy test and a friend asks how it went.

quests.hint: A plan sounds simple but is hard to carry out.
quests.explanation: Great answer to advice you can't follow. It's polite and sympathetic.
quests.meaning: An idiom saying something sounds easy but is hard in practice.
quests.sampleUsage: Wake up at five every day? That's easier said than done.
quests.instruction: Say it with a wry, honest tone.
quests.situationExample: Your friend advises you to exercise every morning before work.

quests.hint: The idea might be too ambitious or too big a claim.
quests.explanation: It shows doubt without being rude. The feel is polite and moderate.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying something is possible but not very realistic.
quests.sampleUsage: Finishing the project by Friday is a bit of a stretch.
quests.correctAnswer: It's a bit of a stretch
quests.expression: It's a bit of a stretch
quests.textToSpeak: It's a bit of a stretch
quests.instruction: Say it thoughtfully and calmly.
quests.situationExample: Your manager asks if the team can finish everything by Friday.

quests.hint: You'll solve the problem yourself.
quests.explanation: "Figure out" means to find an answer by thinking. It sounds calm and confident.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying you'll find a solution on your own.
quests.sampleUsage: I've never used this app, but I'll figure it out.
quests.instruction: Say it confidently, without stress.
quests.situationExample: Your cousin offers help, but you want to try the new app alone.

quests.hint: You want to solve a problem together.
quests.explanation: "Sort out" is British but understood widely. It's friendly and practical.
quests.meaning: A phrase for solving a problem or confusion.
quests.sampleUsage: There's a misunderstanding. Let's sort this out.
quests.instruction: Say it in a friendly, problem-solving tone.
quests.situationExample: Two coworkers have different versions of the same schedule.

quests.hint: You reassure someone with confidence.
quests.explanation: It doesn't promise anything specific but shows support. Register: warm, optimistic.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying a situation will end well.
quests.sampleUsage: Don't worry. Things will work out.
quests.instruction: Say it warmly and gently.
quests.situationExample: A friend is worried about finding a new job.

quests.hint: You met someone unexpectedly.
quests.explanation: "Run into" means to meet by chance. Similar to "bump into".
quests.meaning: A phrase for meeting someone unexpectedly.
quests.sampleUsage: Guess what? I ran into an old friend at the airport.
quests.correctAnswer: I ran into an old friend
quests.expression: I ran into an old friend
quests.textToSpeak: I ran into an old friend
quests.instruction: Say it with a cheerful tone, as a story.
quests.situationExample: You come home from the airport and your roommate asks why you're smiling.

quests.hint: You'll think of an idea.
quests.explanation: "Come up with" means to create or find an idea. Perfect for brainstorming.
quests.meaning: A phrase to say you'll produce an idea.
quests.sampleUsage: Let me come up with something before the weekend.
quests.correctAnswer: Let me come up with something
quests.expression: Let me come up with something
quests.textToSpeak: Let me come up with something
quests.instruction: Say it in a relaxed, confident tone.
quests.situationExample: Your teammate asks for ideas for a gift.

quests.hint: You feel happy about something coming.
quests.explanation: Followed by a noun or -ing form. It's polite and positive.
quests.meaning: A phrase showing you're happy about a future event.
quests.sampleUsage: That sounds great. I'm looking forward to it.
quests.instruction: Say it warmly, with anticipation.
quests.situationExample: An interviewer says the next step is a short team meeting next week.

quests.hint: Your goal: to talk properly after a long time.
quests.explanation: "Catch up" means to share news. Very common among friends.
quests.meaning: A phrase suggesting a meeting to share news.
quests.sampleUsage: It's been ages. Let's catch up soon!
quests.instruction: Say it warmly, as a quick goodbye between friends.
quests.situationExample: You meet an old friend for five minutes at a bus stop.

quests.hint: You'd like a casual social plan.
quests.explanation: Informal, friendly, and often vague. Add a day to make it real.
quests.meaning: A phrase suggesting you spend time together.
quests.sampleUsage: We should hang out sometime this weekend.
quests.instruction: Say it in a casual, friendly tone.
quests.situationExample: A new classmate mentions she likes the same band as you.

quests.hint: You suggest a more planned meeting.
quests.explanation: Slightly more planned than "hang out". Use it with friends, family or teams.
quests.meaning: A suggestion to meet as a group.
quests.sampleUsage: Let's get together this weekend for dinner.
quests.instruction: Say it cheerfully, as an invitation.
quests.situationExample: You're back in your hometown for a few days and your cousins live nearby.

quests.hint: Here you'd like to act now.
quests.explanation: "Put off" means to delay. It's direct and motivating.
quests.meaning: A phrase suggesting you shouldn't delay something.
quests.sampleUsage: We keep talking about it. Let's not put it off any longer.
quests.instruction: Say it firmly but kindly.
quests.situationExample: You and your sister keep postponing a visit to your grandparents.

quests.hint: An event was canceled.
quests.explanation: "Call off" means to cancel something planned. Often used for sports and events.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying an event was canceled.
quests.sampleUsage: They called off the match because of the storm.
quests.instruction: Say it as news, in a neutral tone.
quests.situationExample: You explain to your friend why the football game didn't happen.

quests.hint: You're reducing something.
quests.explanation: "Cut down on" means to reduce. Good for habits and health.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying you're reducing your use of something.
quests.sampleUsage: I'm trying to cut down on sugar, so just half a spoon.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm trying to cut down on sugar
quests.expression: I'm trying to cut down on sugar
quests.textToSpeak: I'm trying to cut down on sugar
quests.instruction: Explain it casually while you turn the sugar down.
quests.situationExample: A friend offers sugar for your tea.

quests.hint: You decide to stop for now.
quests.explanation: Common at work and study. It signals you've done enough.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying you'll stop working.
quests.sampleUsage: We've done enough. Let's call it a day.
quests.instruction: Say it in a tired, friendly tone.
quests.situationExample: It's late evening and you and a colleague have finished the main work.

quests.hint: You need time overnight to decide.
quests.explanation: It shows you take the choice seriously. Perfect for big decisions.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying you'll decide tomorrow.
quests.sampleUsage: It's a big offer. Let me sleep on it.
quests.instruction: Say it calmly, as a polite pause.
quests.situationExample: A landlord asks if you want to rent the apartment now.

quests.hint: You'll decide as things develop.
quests.explanation: It suggests you don't need a fixed plan. Best described as relaxed and flexible.
quests.meaning: An idiom meaning you'll decide later based on events.
quests.sampleUsage: I'm not sure about dinner. Let's play it by ear.
quests.instruction: Say it as a flexible, easygoing plan.
quests.situationExample: Your roommate wants exact plans, but the weather might change.

quests.hint: Picture yourself trying to calm someone worried about a problem.
quests.explanation: Friendly reassurance. It says the problem isn't as big as it feels.
quests.meaning: An idiom saying a problem is not so serious.
quests.sampleUsage: You missed one class. It's not the end of the world.
quests.correctAnswer: It's not the end of the world
quests.expression: It's not the end of the world
quests.textToSpeak: It's not the end of the world
quests.instruction: Say it kindly, with a small smile.
quests.situationExample: A friend is upset after she missed a class.

quests.hint: You suggest a positive view.
quests.explanation: Friendly and slightly playful. Avoid using it if someone is truly grieving.
quests.meaning: A phrase encouraging someone to see something positive.
quests.sampleUsage: The flight was late, but look on the bright side, we saw the city at night.
quests.instruction: Say it kindly, with a gentle smile.
quests.situationExample: Your trip was delayed, but you got extra time in a nice city.

quests.hint: You want someone to feel better.
quests.explanation: Tone matters: don't use it in serious emotional situations.
quests.meaning: A phrase telling someone to feel happier.
quests.sampleUsage: Cheer up! Tomorrow will be better.
quests.instruction: Say it lightly and warmly.
quests.situationExample: A classmate is sad because her sports team lost.

quests.hint: You quickly connected with someone.
quests.explanation: It's about instant chemistry, whether friendship or a good working relationship.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying you got along well quickly.
quests.sampleUsage: We hit it off right away. We talked for hours.
quests.correctAnswer: We hit it off right away
quests.expression: We hit it off right away
quests.textToSpeak: We hit it off right away
quests.instruction: Say it warmly, as a story.
quests.situationExample: You describe meeting your new roommate to a friend.

quests.hint: You have good relationships with people.
quests.explanation: "Get along with" is natural and positive for describing relationships.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying you have friendly relationships.
quests.sampleUsage: I get along with everyone on my team.
quests.instruction: Say it in a friendly tone.
quests.situationExample: A recruiter asks how you work with colleagues.

quests.hint: You share interests or background.
quests.explanation: A friendly and simple sentence for describing similarities.
quests.meaning: A phrase saying two people share similar interests.
quests.sampleUsage: We have a lot in common. We both love hiking.
quests.correctAnswer: We have a lot in common
quests.expression: We have a lot in common
quests.textToSpeak: We have a lot in common
quests.instruction: Say it with genuine interest.
quests.situationExample: You've been talking to a new neighbor about hobbies.
